about: workflow:keep-community-space-records: keeps a community's membership row, saved configuration, rules, member types and members in the space's own store, every write whole, on the revision it was read at, with a rule row created only once. It replaces the records-door adapter of tools/run-a-community (read-data/community-memberships.mjs: the reads, list, writes, nested transactions, compare-and-swap and the rule defaults), whose decisions are now read-data/community-access.mjs values. Old home: the retired source's src/calendar.json /community/events routes and the community membership methods at source commit b6ae0ebf815f2f5271eed34e6e023c7e1767ec04 (rule a-tool-is-only-what-the-store-cannot-do).

payload.label: Keep community space records
payload.job: Keep a community's membership row, saved configuration, rules, member types and members in the space's own store, each write whole and only on the revision it was read at, a rule row created only once, and read the space back so anyone can see who may be in it and why.
payload.produces: The store's own space objects, proven on the example operations, reads and probes in three kinds of store, and each run's space rows kept, refused and read back.

source.from: the owner, 2026-11-18, and the W3.2b lane brief: run-a-community's records-door adapter kept the space's rows; a tool keeps no record, the store does
source.note: Ported from the retired Worker's community membership adapter (source commit b6ae0ebf815f2f5271eed34e6e023c7e1767ec04; see tools/run-a-community/source-baselines and src/community-membership-record-model.json for the record kinds and their identities). Who may be in a community (join rules, paid access, invitation evidence) stays in the tool as values: tools/run-a-community/read-data/community-access.mjs.

where.description: Where the space is kept: the store's own address, as the person's store row names it

language.description: How that store is spoken to, in its own terms

credential_name.description: The vault name of the login the run uses for that store, when it needs one

place.description: Where in the store the spaces are kept, when the person has a place for them already

labels.description: The label DATA (membership_labels: joined_by and the default configuration per label)

operations.description: Each operation: writes [{type, id, value, expected_revision?}], guards [{type, id}] (optional), in order

reads.description: Each read: {community, relay} for a yes or no on who may be in it

steps.title: Read what the store already keeps
steps.do: Speak to the store in its own language, with the login under its credential_name, and read its own description of what it holds. Submit kept_in (where the spaces are kept, or null) and objects (the names of the objects that already answer each question below).

steps.title: Make the store's own objects, once
steps.do: When the look step found no such objects, make them in the store's own form: (1) one table of space rows (the community's membership row, its saved configuration, its rules, its member types, and its members), each row with a revision the store increments on every change; (2) a rule that a write names the revision it was read at, or that it is new (absent) and that a row that exists is never created again; (3) a rule that a batch is whole or not at all, and that a guard row must still hold the revision it was read at in the same batch; (4) a read of one space's rows. Grant only what the store needs for these.

steps.title: Prove the objects on the example operations
steps.do: In a throwaway place in the same store, with the same objects, run these operations in order, each through the store's own objects: [{"id": "o1", "op": "seed", "writes": [{"type": "membership", "id": "space-1", "value": {"id": "space-1", "label": "community", "title": "A community", "created_by": "relay-owner", "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"}}, {"type": "member", "id": "space-1:relay-member", "value": {"membership_id": "space-1", "relay": "relay-member", "role": "member", "state": "member", "changed_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"}}]}, {"id": "o2", "op": "save-config", "writes": [{"type": "community", "id": "space-1", "value": {"id": "space-1", "config": {"join": [{"invited": true}], "spaces": {"events": "members"}}, "created_at": "2026-01-02T00:00:00.000Z", "updated_at": "2026-01-03T00:00:00.000Z"}}]}, {"id": "o3", "op": "ensure-rules", "writes": [{"type": "rules", "id": "space-1", "value": {"id": "space-1", "rules": "Be kind", "changed_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"}}]}, {"id": "o4", "op": "ensure-rules-again", "writes": [{"type": "rules", "id": "space-1", "value": {"id": "space-1", "rules": "Other", "changed_at": "2026-01-05T00:00:00.000Z"}, "expected_revision": null}]}, {"id": "o5", "op": "member-type", "writes": [{"type": "own_member_type", "id": "space-1:coach", "value": {"space_id": "space-1", "type_id": "coach", "label": "Coach", "inherits": []}}]}, {"id": "o6", "op": "join-with-guard", "writes": [{"type": "member", "id": "space-1:relay-two", "value": {"membership_id": "space-1", "relay": "relay-two", "role": "member", "state": "member", "changed_at": "2026-01-06T00:00:00.000Z"}}], "guards": [{"type": "member", "id": "space-1:relay-member"}]}, {"id": "o7", "op": "stale-config", "writes": [{"type": "community", "id": "space-1", "value": {"id": "space-1", "config": {"join": [{"free": true}]}, "created_at": "2026-01-02T00:00:00.000Z", "updated_at": "2026-01-07T00:00:00.000Z"}, "expected_revision": 0}]}] Then read the space's rows and the decisions the planning values give for each read ([{"id": "r1", "community": "space-1", "relay": "relay-member"}, {"id": "r2", "community": "space-1", "relay": "relay-two"}, {"id": "r3", "community": "space-1", "relay": "relay-absent"}]), and try each probe ([{"id": "p1", "op": "insert-existing-membership", "id_of": "space-1"}, {"id": "p2", "op": "guard-moved", "id_of": "space-1:relay-member"}]). Submit results, refusals (each operation refused and the store's words), rows (every row read back, with its revision), community, decisions, and probes (refused or changed).

checks.says: Every example operation is kept or refused as the intent says, every probe is refused, and the store's own objects give every expected answer

steps.title: Keep this run's operations
steps.do: For each operation: read the rows it touches, make the batch with each row's revision as read (absent rows as new), write the batch whole and refuse when the store refuses; for a read, give the decision the values in the community-access rules and say whether the person may act and why. Submit results, refused, kept_ids (the rows written), found_ids (every row read back).

checks.says: Every row written is read back
